significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that incomplete enumeration occurs despite a decodable full-set representation because "already-emitted members inhibit the retrieval of remaining ones" and premature stopping follows—a causal mechanism plus a form-(iii) predictive coupling between measurable inhibition, list position, and omission. This would establish both a phenomenon (latent membership and cardinality remain available when answers are omitted) and a mechanism (serialization competition and emitted-member inhibition), fixing expectations that suppression should accumulate across generation and that removing it should recover members rather than merely increasing list length; this is sharper than the single-fact recall framing exemplified by Geva et al. (2023). True and false are distinguishable, while a negative result would meaningfully rule out this specific storage-versus-serialization account but not every possible retrieval bottleneck. In the topic-substitution check, generic questions about why stored knowledge fails would not merit this score; the claim-specific inhibition-to-omission coupling and separation of latent set storage from serialization provide the above-median increment.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed "emitted-member suppression removal" intervention, the decoded "set cardinality," and a "set-cardinality-aware stop calibration"; these are decode-time, ex-ante handles because they act before the model omits a remaining member or emits EOS. Although activation directions require re-extraction, the asserted relation predicts what should recur after recalibration—emitted-member activity suppresses remaining-member retrieval, while cardinality indicates when stopping is premature—rather than supplying only an unexplained model-specific direction. The hypothesis covers finite-set retrieval across geographic, relational, and definitional tasks and offers a training-free control potentially usable by model auditors or inference-system builders, though it does not establish transfer beyond text LLM enumeration or eliminate the need for model-specific calibration. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the generic knowledge-retrieval topic supplies no ex-ante intervention or transferable inhibition relation, whereas these named handles do.
